cards.d: An addict is a person who cannot stop doing or having something.
cards.e: She was a coffee addict. She had more than three cups each day.

cards.d: When something is archeological, it relates to archeology.
cards.e: They found archeological evidence that proved an ancient species of man.

cards.d: Archeology is the study of ancient people through their artifacts.
cards.e: He studied archeology to learn more about ancient Egyptian culture.

cards.d: To brainstorm is to have a lot of ideas about a certain topic.
cards.e: The students met after school to brainstorm ideas for their assignment.

cards.d: A budget is the amount of money available to spend on something.
cards.e: His budget for food was very tight.

cards.d: When something is chaotic, it is crazy, confused, and hectic.
cards.e: The first day of school can be chaotic for a new student.

cards.d: To cite something is to mention it as an example or as proof of something.
cards.e: She cited six reasons that the school needed to build new classrooms.

cards.d: To correspond is to match or to be similar to something.
cards.e: The boy’s story didn’t correspond with his mother’s version.

cards.d: A courtyard is an outdoor area that is surrounded by the walls of a building.
cards.e: During the summer, the courtyard is a nice place to have lunch.

cards.d: An estate is a large area of land owned by a family or organization.
cards.e: He lived on his father’s estate in the country.

cards.d: Fraud is the crime of gaining money by lying or by tricking people.
cards.e: Experts say that credit card fraud increases around the holidays.

cards.d: Hydrogen is a gas that has no taste, color, or smell.
cards.e: Balloons filled with hydrogen can easily float away if you aren’t careful.

cards.d: Integrity is honesty and good morals.
cards.e: The principal had a lot of integrity.

cards.d: To knit is to make fabric by connecting strings together.
cards.e: My grandmother knitted me a sweater.

cards.d: An outlook is a person’s opinion or way of thinking about something.
cards.e: He changed his outlook about rats after he read a book about them.

cards.d: A parachute is a device that helps people and things fall to the ground safely.
cards.e: They used parachutes dropped from airplanes to send supplies to the civilians.

cards.d: When something is prehistoric, it is from a time when there was no written history.
cards.e: The scientists found prehistoric pots used by the people in the area.

cards.d: A proponent is a person who supports an idea or a plan.
cards.e: He was a proponent of using environmentally friendly products.

cards.d: To refine something is to make it better by making changes.
cards.e: The principal refined his method of controlling students over the years.

cards.d: To restrict is to limit something and prevent it from getting bigger.
cards.e: The club restricted the amount of members.
